items.title: Thefacebook
items.line: Mark Zuckerberg and his Harvard roommates launched TheFacebook on 4 February 2004. It was Harvard-only at first, built around the printed student directories called face books.

items.title: Shaun of the Dead
items.line: Edgar Wright's zombie comedy opened in UK cinemas on 9 April 2004, on a budget of about 4 million pounds. The pub fight is cued to Queen's "Don't Stop Me Now".

items.title: Garden State
items.line: Zach Braff wrote, directed and starred in it on a $2.5 million budget. It premiered at Sundance on 16 January 2004 and its hand-picked soundtrack went on to win a Grammy.

items.title: Athens Olympics
items.line: The Games came home to Greece, running 13 to 29 August 2004 with 201 nations taking part. It was Athens' first time hosting since the first modern Games in 1896.

items.title: Lost
items.line: Lost debuted on ABC on 22 September 2004, after a pilot that reportedly cost $10 to $14 million. Oceanic 815 crashed on a Hawaiian beach, and season one averaged about 15.7 million viewers.

items.title: Half-Life 2
items.line: Valve released Half-Life 2 on 16 November 2004, and you had to have Steam running to play it, which annoyed plenty of people. The gravity gun made the physics the fun part.

items.title: Nintendo DS
items.line: The Nintendo DS arrived in North America on 21 November 2004 at US$149.99, with two screens and a touch screen on the bottom. It went on to sell about 154 million units.
